properties.decision:
Anthony, 2026-08-30: *"it sounds like the alternative is not viable, so I think a brainstormed idea becomes a first class kind in the vocabulary."* Shape (ii) chosen the same day: A DECLARED PROPERTY ON `Decision`, not a new node type.

WHAT THIS SETTLES, AND ONLY THIS. An exploratory idea gets a declared, queryable marker distinguishing it from a Decision recording a choice somebody faced. It does NOT settle `dec:exploratory-staging`'s second half — where a NOT-YET-AGREED WISH lives (the Capability side, 34 stuck gaps, added 2026-08-10). That node's own closing line names the wish question as the one to put to the user, and it was not put or answered today. It stays open.

═══ WHY NOW, WHEN IT WAS TWICE JUDGED TOO SMALL ═══

`dec:exploratory-staging` recorded that two of the four original arguments for a kind had DISSOLVED — brainstormed ideas are already silent by construction (`detect_gaps` raises `undecided_decision_point` only on a Decision with 2+ registered alternatives), and delivery/certainty counts already exclude Decisions. What remained was retirement candidates and at-a-glance readability: *"real but small"*, and explicitly left to Anthony as a schema-change judgement.

⭐ A THIRD ARGUMENT NOW EXISTS AND IT IS OF A DIFFERENT KIND. `dec:idea-governance-rides-the-tool-that-does-the-thing` proposes A′ — extending the near-match refusal that already fires so it also asks about RELATEDNESS, not only duplication. Measured 2026-08-30, A′ CANNOT BE SCOPED WITHOUT THIS: 207 idea-Decisions and 363 other Decisions differ by NOTHING a computation may read. Status does not separate them (32 non-idea Decisions are also `proposed`); `no_relation_note` is the discipline's output, not a marker available before it exists. The only separator is the `dec:idea-` ID PREFIX.

🛑 AND THAT IS THE DEFECT FIXED AND MERGED THE SAME MORNING. `fact:seam-roll-up-found-a-container-by-id-prefix-and-answered-a-false-zero` (#390): an id's spelling treated as authoritative about what a node IS, instead of asking the graph. Scoping A′ by prefix would reintroduce that class hours after closing it. That is the *"alternative is not viable"* Anthony is referring to.

So the argument that carries this is not readability. It is `req:a-vocabulary-distinction-proves-it-is-read`: a distinction earns its keep when a computation reads it, and A′ is that computation. Unscoped, A′ would land on the Requirement/Capability/ChangeEvent capture path that Alex's 2026-08-30 field report identifies as his existing friction — so the marker is what keeps a fix for idea linking away from a live user's working path.

═══ THE SHAPE, CHOSEN ═══

(i) A NEW NODE TYPE was rejected: everything handling Decision would have to learn it — `what_next`, the detectors, the reports, delivery, the merge driver — for a noun whose behaviour is otherwise identical.

(ii) CHOSEN — a declared property on `Decision`, set by the brainstorm skill at capture and read by the guard. It buys the computation A′ needs and both benefits `dec:exploratory-staging` was holding out for: retirement candidates and readability become queries rather than prose. Model it on `Decision.quality_target`, whose own description settles the default question correctly — ABSENT MEANS NOBODY WAS ASKED, never a substantive value.

⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-30, AFTER THE CHOICE AND BEFORE THE BUILD. This node first said the stamp trap applies *"if the marker is expressed as an ENUM VALUE"*. THAT WAS INCOMPLETE AND THE CORRECTION MATTERS TO (ii). The export stamp carries `node_type_names`, `edge_type_names` and their counts — AND NO PROPERTY NAMES AT ALL. So a new PROPERTY is equally invisible to it, whichever way the marker is shaped; the hazard is not enum-specific and cannot be dodged by choosing a bool. This project has recorded four instances of that blindness, most recently on `ifc:mcp-tools-http`, where a missing enum word was declined once for exactly this reason before being added anyway. A consumer pinning a build gains a distinction nothing tells them about. `schema_version` (currently 1) is the field that COULD carry it; whether it is bumped for a property addition is not established and is the one thing to check while building.

═══ NOT ESTABLISHED ═══
· Whether existing idea-Decisions get backfilled, and on what evidence. The only signal available for the existing 207 is the id prefix — the very thing being retired — so a backfill would launder it into a property. Marking only NEW ideas is honest and leaves the old population unqueryable; backfilling is convenient and dishonest. Nobody has chosen.
· Whether `schema_version` moves for a property addition (above).
· Whether the marker belongs on Decision at all, or whether the wish question (`dec:exploratory-staging`, 2026-08-10 half) wants the same mechanism, in which case deciding them separately may foreclose one.
properties.name: DECIDED — a brainstormed idea is a first-class kind in the vocabulary, because the alternative is an id-prefix test
properties.rationale: Recorded as its own accepted Decision rather than by moving `dec:exploratory-staging` to accepted, because that node holds TWO questions and Anthony answered one. Marking it accepted would assert that the not-yet-agreed-wish half — its 2026-08-10 addition, 34 stuck gaps, and the question its own text names as the one to put to the user — had been settled today. It was not.
